answer: LINE (Large-scale Information Network Embedding) defines the second-order proximity objective O2 so that each vertex i has a weighting term λ_i that scales its contribution to the loss. In the original formulation, λ_i is set from the vertex out-degree, so higher-out-degree vertices contribute more strongly during optimization. In the reported experiments, the authors also consider replacing the out-degree-based weighting with PageRank scores, using PageRank as an alternative importance measure for vertices. Conceptually, this means λ_i is computed from each vertex’s PageRank value rather than from its out-degree, and the optimization of O2 then proceeds with those PageRank-derived weights. The practical effect is to bias training toward vertices that are more central under PageRank, instead of vertices that merely have many outgoing edges. This is an experimental weighting choice rather than a change to the core LINE objective itself.
